source_read: PMC HTML, PMC8459304: Key Points, abstract, Introduction, Methods, all Results subsections, Tables 1-4 (HTML), Discussion, Limitations and Conclusions read in full (Tables 3-4 read in step 2 to check the card). Figure (image) not inspected; supplementary eTable (PDF) not opened.

claims.note: Every number checks against Table 1 (adults 18-64): any use 1,612k (1,394-1,829) in 2015 to 1,971k (1,660-2,282) in 2019, P for trend .002; MUD 741k (578-905) to 1,091k (816-1,365), P .003; psychostimulant (T43.6) deaths 5,526 to 15,489, 8,438 with opioids in 2019. Editors' calculations recomputed: use +22.3%, MUD +47.2%, deaths +180.3%, opioid-involved share 54.5% ('more than half'). The critique of the headline figures is correct and in fact understated: besides use (+43%, 1,381k in 2016 as base) and MUD without injection (+105%, 397k in 2016), the paper's MUD +62% (672k, 2016), frequent use +66% (615k, 2016), use without opioids +61% and without opioids or cocaine +58% (2016 bases), and use without MUD or injection +42% (556k, 2017 base) are all computed from the lowest year while described as 2015-2019 changes; only cocaine co-use (+60%) and frequent use without MUD or injection (+108%) start at 2015. From 2015, MUD without injection rose 48% and frequent use 57%. The Discussion's contrast of a 180% rise in deaths with a 43% rise in use therefore understates the gap (22% from 2015).

anchors.locator: Table 1, overdose-death rows; Results > Trends in Psychostimulant-Involved Overdose Deaths
anchors.extracted: Deaths among people aged 18-64 with ICD-10 T43.6 (psychostimulants other than cocaine) and an overdose underlying cause: 5,526 (2015), 7,301, 10,029, 12,203, 15,489 (2019), +180%, P<.001; with opioids 2,306 to 8,438 (+266%); without opioids 3,220 to 7,051.

NSDUH 2015-2019, 195,711 respondents aged 18-64; MUD by DSM-IV criteria; trend analysis limited to 2015-2019 because of a 2015 methods break; mean weighted screening response 75.3% and interview response 67.3%.

anchors.locator: Abstract > Results; Key Points; Results > Trends in Methamphetamine Use, Co-Use, MUD, and Injection; Results > Trends in Frequent Methamphetamine Use
anchors.extracted: Paper's stated 2015-2019 increases use non-2015 bases: use 43% (1.4 to 2.0 million = 2016 to 2019), MUD 62% (672k, 2016), MUD without injection 105% (397k, 2016), frequent use 66% (615k, 2016), use without MUD or injection 42% (556k, 2017).

Cross-sectional; NSDUH excludes people experiencing homelessness outside shelters and institutionalized people (e.g., in jail or prison), so prevalence is likely underestimated; self-report; about 85-90% of T43.6 death certificates mention methamphetamine; some certificates name no specific drug (6% in 2019).

key_findings.correction: All 17 adjusted risk ratios checked against Table 3 (middle column).
Checked against Table 3 (right column); ages 35-49 and 50-64: 4.07 and 4.20.

The first three limitations are in Discussion > Limitations, but the statement that overdose counts omit deaths from methamphetamine-associated conditions (stroke, myocardial infarction, pulmonary hypertension, HIV/AIDS, hepatitis) and markedly underestimate mortality is in the Discussion's 7th paragraph (the COVID-19 paragraph), not in the Limitations subsection. The Limitations subsection also contains the 85-90% methamphetamine-mention and 6% unspecified-drug figures, which the card places in KF1's note.

reporting_issues.note: Found independently in step 1. Recomputed: any use +22.3% (2015) vs +42.7% (2016); MUD +47.2% vs +62.4%; MUD without injection +48.5% vs +105.3%; frequent use +57.3% vs +66.0%; without opioid misuse +20.7%; without opioids or cocaine +8.7%.
Results > Increases in Adjusted Past-Year Prevalence of MUD Without Injection opens by saying years were combined (2015-2017 vs 2018-2019).
The card's remark that the Figure shows standard errors was not checked (Figure not inspected).

The rule the paper follows is simpler than 'whichever year differed significantly': in every case the baseline is the lowest year of the series (2016 for use, MUD, MUD without injection, frequent use, use without opioids, use without opioids or cocaine; 2017 for use without MUD or injection; 2015 where 2015 was lowest, e.g., cocaine co-use and frequent use without MUD or injection). For any use, MUD and frequent use, 2015 is also flagged as significantly different from 2019 but was not used.

risk_of_bias.note: JBI prevalence checklist domains agreed; 'moderate' overall is reasonable for the survey estimates. The selective-baseline problem affects the paper's text, not the Table 1 estimates the claim uses.

interpretation_gap.note: Also: the Discussion's contrast of a 180% rise in deaths with a '43%' rise in use understates the divergence, since use rose 22% from 2015.

missed: Table 3, injection column, nicotine dependence: ARR 1.87 (1.37-3.54) is asymmetric on the log scale; the upper bound is probably a misprint (2.54 would be symmetric).
Table 4, 2015 adjusted prevalence of frequent use: 41.56% (25.55-47.83); the lower bound is implausibly far from the estimate compared with every other row and is probably a misprint (e.g., 35.55).

For cl_meth_us_trends: the death counts are restricted to decedents aged 18-64 (Results, first paragraph; Table 1 title), matching the survey age range; the claim's 'Among US adults aged 18-64' therefore covers both series correctly.
